_comment: Per-chart narratives. CI (build_prompt.py -> GitHub Models -> write_narrative.py) overwrites these from live numbers; this committed copy is the fallback so the page always reads well. source = 'fallback' | 'github-models'.

notes.fossil: As of June 2026, WTI crude oil is priced at $84.38 per barrel, Brent crude at $86.99 per barrel, and US regular gasoline at $4.00 per gallon, while Henry Hub natural gas trades at $2.8 per MMBtu. Among these fuels, natural gas has exhibited the greatest volatility, as indicated by an indexed comparison to 2019 where natural gas spiked most sharply in 2022 before moderating. Crude oil and gasoline prices have moved more closely together, reflecting more stable correlation in their market dynamics. This elevated volatility in natural gas prices stems from supply-demand fluctuations and market sensitivity to global and regional factors.
notes.transition: The levelised cost of electricity (LCOE), which represents the average cost per megawatt-hour (MWh) of building and operating a generating plant over its lifetime, currently shows solar photovoltaic (PV) at $44/MWh and onshore wind at $33/MWh. These costs are lower than new offshore wind at $75/MWh, gas combined cycle gas turbine (CCGT) at $76/MWh, and coal at $110/MWh. The significant drop in solar PV’s LCOE—about a 90% reduction from approximately $460/MWh in 2010 to $44/MWh today—demonstrates the rapid cost improvements and efficiency gains in solar technology. As a result, solar PV and onshore wind now provide more economical options for new electricity generation compared to fossil fuel-based sources.
notes.currency: The estimated share of global oil trade settled outside the US dollar is about 20% and rising, although this figure is unofficial and subject to estimation uncertainty. Despite this gradual diversification, the US dollar continues to dominate oil trade settlements worldwide. This slow drift away from dollar dominance is primarily driven by Russia’s pivot to Asian buyers and increased use of alternative currencies such as the Chinese yuan and Indian rupee for settling oil cargoes. These developments reflect changing geopolitical and economic relationships rather than a definitive shift away from dollar-based trade.
notes.now: Current energy prices reflect a complex interplay of traditional fossil fuel markets, evolving renewable cost structures, and shifting financial settlement practices. Fossil fuels maintain significant price stability in oil and gasoline but exhibit high volatility in natural gas. At the same time, renewable energy sources, notably solar PV and onshore wind, have become cost-competitive alternatives based on levelised cost metrics. Meanwhile, the currency composition of oil trade settlements shows a gradual, estimated rise in non-dollar use, illustrating subtle shifts in global trade dynamics.
